chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Any believer who presents a believer in a dispute to a judge or an unjust ruler, and he judges against him contrary to the judgment of Allah, has shared in the sin."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on referring a believer to an unjust judge in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the moral weight of *tawliyah* (referencing) to unjust authorities (*al-sulta al-ja'ir*), warning that the referent shares in the sin of the judge's deviation from divine law. It serves as a critical criterion for evaluating the validity of judicial referrals in the absence of the Infallible Imam, emphasizing that procedural correctness is insufficient if substantive justice is compromised.
